quests.hint: THE PILE OF DIRTY CLOTHES YOU WASH, DRY, AND FOLD
quests.explanation: We say DO THE LAUNDRY, not 'make the laundry.' DO is the verb for everyday chores and tasks — do the laundry, do the shopping, do the cleaning — while MAKE is for creating something, like a meal or a plan.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: The washing machine broke last week, so I still need to do the ___ by hand.

quests.hint: STRAIGHTENING YOUR SHEETS AND PILLOW SO THE ROOM LOOKS TIDY
quests.explanation: MAKE YOUR BED is the standard phrase for tidying it after you sleep. MAKE combines with things you form or arrange, while chores like sweeping or vacuuming usually take DO.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that forms a natural pair.
quests.contextSentence: Before you leave for school, please make your ___.

quests.hint: MOVING THE BAGS OF HOUSEHOLD WASTE OUTSIDE FOR COLLECTION
quests.explanation: TAKE OUT THE TRASH means to carry the household waste outside, usually to a bin. In British English, people more often say 'put out the rubbish,' but TAKE OUT THE TRASH is standard in American English.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this everyday task.
quests.contextSentence: Could you take out the ___ before the truck comes on Monday morning?

quests.hint: TWO SLICES OF BREAD WITH SOMETHING TASTY IN BETWEEN
quests.explanation: MAKE A SANDWICH is the natural phrase for preparing this simple food. MAKE is used broadly for preparing food from ingredients — make a sandwich, make a salad, make soup.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: There was no time to cook, so she decided to make a quick ___ for lunch.

quests.hint: COOKING SOMETHING IN BUBBLING WATER UNTIL THE SHELL AND INSIDE ARE FIRM
quests.explanation: BOIL AN EGG means to cook it in hot water. BOIL is the verb we use for cooking something by putting it directly in water that is bubbling, such as boil pasta or boil vegetables.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that matches this cooking method.
wrongCollocations: cook an EGG in the oven
quests.contextSentence: For breakfast, my dad always likes to boil an ___ and eat it with toast.

quests.hint: ARRANGING PLATES, GLASSES, AND CUTLERY BEFORE A MEAL BEGINS
quests.explanation: SET THE TABLE means to arrange the plates and cutlery for a meal. SET is also used for other arrangements, like set a goal or set an alarm, where you put something in place ahead of time.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this mealtime routine.
quests.contextSentence: As soon as the guests arrived, the children rushed to set the ___ for dinner.

quests.hint: SCHOOLWORK YOU COMPLETE AT HOME, USUALLY ASSIGNED BY A TEACHER
quests.explanation: DO HOMEWORK is the fixed expression for completing schoolwork outside class. DO pairs with tasks and duties, while a finished written piece, like an essay, is something you WRITE.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: My son usually does his ___ right after dinner, before he watches any television.

quests.hint: LIFTING PART OF YOUR BODY IN CLASS TO SHOW YOU WANT TO SPEAK
quests.explanation: RAISE YOUR HAND is the classroom expression for signaling you want to answer or ask something. RAISE can also combine with your voice or a concern, but never with a whole arm gesture like waving.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that fits this classroom action.
quests.contextSentence: If you know the answer, raise your ___ instead of shouting it out.

quests.hint: GIVING YOUR COMPLETED WORK TO THE TEACHER BY A CERTAIN DATE
quests.explanation: HAND IN AN ASSIGNMENT means to submit your completed work. HAND IN is commonly used for schoolwork and forms, while HAND OUT means the opposite — giving copies to a group of people.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this school routine.
quests.contextSentence: Students must hand in their ___ by Friday afternoon, or points will be deducted.

quests.hint: BOARDING PUBLIC TRANSPORT ON TIME, BEFORE IT LEAVES WITHOUT YOU
quests.explanation: CATCH THE TRAIN means to arrive in time to board it. CATCH works for scheduled transport you might otherwise miss — catch a train, catch a flight, catch a bus.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: If we leave now, we should still catch the seven o'clock ___ to the city.

quests.hint: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU ARRIVE AT THE AIRPORT TOO LATE
quests.explanation: MISS THE FLIGHT means you arrive after it has already departed. MISS is the opposite of CATCH in this sense — you can miss a flight, a bus, or an important meeting.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this travel mishap.
quests.contextSentence: Because of the traffic jam, they nearly missed their ___ to Rome.

quests.hint: STEPPING UP AND INSIDE A LARGE VEHICLE YOU SHARE WITH OTHER PASSENGERS
quests.explanation: GET ON THE BUS is correct for vehicles you stand and walk into, like buses, trains, or planes. Smaller vehicles you sit down directly into, like a car or taxi, instead use GET IN.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this kind of vehicle.
quests.contextSentence: The doors were closing, so she had to run to get on the ___ in time.

quests.hint: STANDING UNDER RUNNING WATER TO WASH YOUR WHOLE BODY
quests.explanation: TAKE A SHOWER is the standard phrase in English. TAKE combines with many daily routines that don't involve creating anything, such as take a nap or take a break.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: After the gym, he always likes to take a quick ___ before heading home.

quests.hint: PUTTING ON YOUR CLOTHES SO YOU'RE READY TO LEAVE THE HOUSE
quests.explanation: GET DRESSED means to put on your clothes. GET combines naturally with adjectives describing a change of state — get dressed, get ready, get tired — rather than MAKE or DO.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this morning routine.
quests.contextSentence: We're leaving in ten minutes, so please get ___ as quickly as you can.

quests.hint: RUNNING A TOOL WITH BRISTLES THROUGH THE STRANDS ON YOUR HEAD
quests.explanation: BRUSH YOUR HAIR is the natural collocation for this grooming habit. BRUSH also pairs with teeth, but the tool and motion for hair is usually described the same way.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this grooming action.
wrongCollocations: comb your HAIR forcefully with a brush of paint
wash your HAIR with a brush
quests.contextSentence: She likes to brush her ___ in front of the mirror before school.

quests.hint: PAYING WITH PHYSICAL NOTES AND COINS INSTEAD OF A CARD
quests.explanation: PAY IN CASH is the fixed way to describe this payment method. English uses IN with CASH, but BY with CARD or CHEQUE — pay by card, pay by cheque.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: The small market stall only accepts payment in ___, so bring some notes.

quests.hint: PUTTING ON A GARMENT IN THE FITTING ROOM TO CHECK THE FIT
quests.explanation: TRY ON A JACKET means to put it on briefly to see if it fits or suits you, without buying it yet. TRY ON is used specifically for clothes and shoes before a purchase.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this shopping routine.
quests.contextSentence: Before buying it, she asked if she could try on the ___ in a larger size.

quests.hint: TAKING SOMETHING BACK TO THE SHOP BECAUSE IT'S THE WRONG SIZE OR FAULTY
quests.explanation: RETURN AN ITEM means to bring purchased goods back to the store, usually for a refund or exchange. RETURN pairs with things you give back, unlike EXCHANGE, which specifically means swapping for something else.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this customer-service scenario.
wrongCollocations: give back an ITEM to store
quests.contextSentence: If the shoes don't fit, you can return the ___ within thirty days for a full refund.

quests.hint: PICKING UP THE DEVICE THAT'S RINGING AND SPEAKING TO WHOEVER IS CALLING
quests.explanation: ANSWER THE PHONE means to pick it up and respond when it rings. ANSWER also pairs with a question or the door, whenever someone is waiting for a response.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: pick the PHONE up to reply
quests.contextSentence: She was in the shower, so she couldn't answer the ___ when it rang.

quests.hint: TYPING A SHORT NOTE ON YOUR PHONE AND DELIVERING IT INSTANTLY
quests.explanation: SEND A MESSAGE means to transmit a written note electronically, such as a text or app message. SEND is used when the message reaches someone directly and immediately.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this communication method.
quests.contextSentence: Instead of calling, just send a quick ___ so I know you arrived safely.

quests.hint: RECORDING A SPOKEN NOTE BECAUSE THE PERSON DIDN'T PICK UP
quests.explanation: LEAVE A MESSAGE means to record spoken information for someone, typically as voicemail, when they don't answer. Unlike SEND A MESSAGE, this implies the message stays waiting for the other person.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this phone scenario.
wrongCollocations: send a MESSAGE on the recorder
quests.contextSentence: No one picked up, so I decided to leave a ___ explaining why I called.

quests.hint: TAKING YOUR PET OUTSIDE ON A LEASH FOR SOME EXERCISE
quests.explanation: WALK THE DOG describes taking a pet outside for exercise. WALK is also used with people, as in walk a friend home, but not typically with pets that don't move on a leash, like cats.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: walk with the DOG on a chair
quests.contextSentence: Every evening before dinner, my brother takes turns to walk the ___ around the block.

quests.hint: FILLING A PET'S BOWL WITH FOOD AT MEALTIMES
quests.explanation: FEED THE CAT is the natural phrase for giving a pet its food. FEED is used broadly for animals and babies, describing the act of giving them something to eat.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this pet-care routine.
quests.contextSentence: Don't forget to feed the ___ before you leave for work this morning.

quests.hint: TAKING CARE OF A YOUNGER FAMILY MEMBER WHILE THE PARENTS ARE OUT
quests.explanation: LOOK AFTER YOUR BROTHER means to supervise and take care of him temporarily. LOOK AFTER is a broad, everyday phrase for caring for people, pets, or even plants while someone else is away.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this family responsibility.
quests.contextSentence: Their mother asked the older sister to look after her little ___ for the afternoon.

quests.hint: USING A CAMERA OR PHONE TO CAPTURE AN IMAGE OF SOMETHING
quests.explanation: TAKE A PHOTO is the natural collocation for capturing an image. TAKE pairs with photo, picture, and video, describing the simple act of recording an image with a device.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: Could you take a ___ of us in front of the fountain before we leave?

quests.hint: TAKING PART IN AN ACTIVITY FOR FUN, OFTEN WITH RULES OR A BOARD
quests.explanation: PLAY A GAME is the standard collocation for this kind of fun activity. PLAY is used for games and sports, while activities without rules, like painting or reading, use different verbs.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this leisure activity.
wrongCollocations: make a GAME to have fun
quests.contextSentence: On rainy afternoons, the kids like to play a board ___ together at the kitchen table.

quests.hint: HEADING OUTSIDE TO MOVE AT A CALM, UNHURRIED PACE — NOT A FAST ONE
quests.explanation: GO FOR A WALK is the right choice here because the context rules out anything faster. GO FOR pairs with several activities — a walk, a run, a swim — but only the context tells you which one fits.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this specific situation.
quests.contextSentence: Since it was already dark outside, they decided to go for a calm ___ instead of jogging.

quests.hint: SWALLOWING A PILL OR SYRUP THAT A DOCTOR HAS PRESCRIBED
quests.explanation: TAKE MEDICINE is the standard phrase for consuming a prescribed remedy. TAKE is used broadly with medicine, pills, and vitamins, describing the act of consuming them.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
quests.contextSentence: The doctor told him to take the ___ twice a day, after breakfast and dinner.

quests.hint: GETTING A MILD ILLNESS, OFTEN WITH A COUGH AND A RUNNY NOSE
quests.explanation: CATCH A COLD means to become infected with this common illness. CATCH is used for illnesses you get from others, such as catch a cold or catch the flu, unlike serious diseases you might DEVELOP.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this common illness.
quests.contextSentence: She always seems to catch a ___ whenever the seasons change.

quests.hint: SLEEPING OR RELAXING ENOUGH SO YOUR BODY RECOVERS ITS ENERGY
quests.explanation: GET SOME REST means to relax or sleep so your body can recover. GET combines with REST the way it does with sleep and energy — describing something you obtain rather than create.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this piece of advice.
quests.contextSentence: The doctor advised him to get plenty of ___ and drink lots of water.
